key_insight: HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC reduced oxidation weight gain by 95.71% relative to bare SA516 boiler steel during 50 cycles at 900°C.
engineering_relevance: Ni–Cr-based coatings, particularly HVOF-sprayed Ni–20Cr+40TiC, show promise for protecting boiler steel against high-temperature oxidation.
method: Applied Ni–20Cr, Ni–20Cr+40TiC, and Ni–20Cr+40TiN coatings using HVOF and plasma spraying.
Characterized microstructure and phases using XRD, SEM/EDS, and X-ray mapping.
evidence_signal: Bare steel exhibited severe oxide spalling and cracking, while coating protection was attributed to dense Cr₂O₃, TiO₂, NiTiO₄, and NiO scales, reduced porosity, and enhanced microhardness.
watch_item: Laboratory air-oxidation results do not establish long-term durability under boiler-service corrosion, erosion, or thermal loading.
paper_title: Microstructure and high-temperature oxidation behaviour of HVOF and plasma sprayed Ni–Cr-based ceramic coatings on SA516 boiler steel
